planting.note: Plant divisions or plugs in spring into consistently wet to saturated, acidic sandy or peaty soil in sun to part shade; this evergreen clumping sedge is a signature understory grass of Carolina bay margins and pocosin-edge wet pine flatwoods from Virginia to the Gulf Coast.

directions: Set divisions or nursery plugs into consistently moist to saturated, acidic soil in part sun to light shade, matching the wet pine flatwoods and pocosin-margin seeps where it grows naturally alongside fetterbush and cinnamon fern. Walter's sedge forms dense, fine-textured evergreen clumps and spreads slowly by short rhizomes, making it a reliable groundcover for rain gardens, pond edges, and bog-garden borders. It tolerates both standing water and brief dry spells once established but colors and fills in best with steady moisture. Cut back old foliage in late winter before new growth emerges to keep clumps tidy.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into saturated, acidic, shaded peat or sandy muck; Collins' sedge is a pocosin and Atlantic white cedar swamp specialist found in shaded bay forest seeps from the mid-Atlantic coastal plain south into the Carolinas.

directions: Plant divisions into saturated, acidic, humus-rich soil in shade to deep part shade, recreating the dim, boggy understory of pocosin pond margins and Atlantic white cedar swamps where this sedge grows beneath fetterbush and sweet pepperbush. It forms loose, arching clumps and is grown less for flowers than for its distinctive inflated, bladdery seed capsules, which add unusual texture to shaded bog-garden plantings in late summer. Keep the crown constantly wet to saturated; it does not tolerate drying out even briefly. This is a specialty item best sourced from native wetland-restoration growers rather than general garden centers.

planting.note: Plant container stock in early spring into moist, acidic, sandy peat; this deciduous blueberry relative is a pocosin and wet-woods shrub of the Atlantic and Gulf coastal plain from Virginia to Florida and Louisiana.

directions: Plant into consistently moist to seasonally wet, acidic sandy soil in full sun to light shade, the same pocosin-margin and wet-woods conditions where it grows with fetterbush, titi, and black highbush blueberry. Clusters of small white to pink-tinged bell flowers open in early spring ahead of the leaves, followed by sweet blue-black berries that ripen earlier than most garden blueberries. It suckers gently to form a loose thicket over time and needs no pruning beyond removing dead wood, but fruits more heavily with a few hours of direct sun. Mulch with pine straw or leaf litter to maintain the acidic, moisture-retentive soil it requires.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into saturated, acidic, nutrient-poor sandy peat in full sun; golden crest is a classic indicator species of Carolina bay margins and pocosin-edge wet pine savannas from New Jersey south to the Carolinas and Gulf coast.

directions: Plant divisions into saturated to consistently wet, acidic, sandy peat in full sun, the same fire-maintained savanna and Carolina bay ecotone conditions that support pitcher plants and sundews. Golden crest sends up grasslike, woolly gray-green basal leaves and tall flower stalks topped with a dense, felted cluster of small gold-yellow flowers in early summer, a texture unlike almost anything else in a bog garden. It spreads slowly by short rhizomes to form sparse colonies and should never be allowed to dry out, since it is adapted to permanently saturated, nutrient-poor ground. Pair it with Carolina redroot and hatpins for an authentic Carolina bay wildflower planting.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into moist to seasonally wet, acidic sandy soil in full sun; St. Peter's-wort is a low semi-evergreen shrub of wet pine flatwoods and pocosin margins across the Atlantic and Gulf coastal plain.

directions: Plant into moist, acidic, sandy soil in full sun to light shade, the open wet pine flatwoods and pocosin-margin conditions where it grows alongside wiregrass and titi. St. Peter's-wort is a compact, semi-woody shrub with distinctive thin, exfoliating cinnamon bark and bright four-petaled yellow flowers held just above the paired bluish-green leaves through summer. It tolerates both seasonally saturated soil and periodic drought once established, and benefits from the same fire or hard pruning cycle that maintains its native savanna habitat, so cutting it back hard every few years keeps it dense and floriferous. Use it as a low accent shrub along the sunny margin of a bog garden or rain garden.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
